newsitem.title: USA: Lone Star Steak sees Q3 net below estimate.
newsitem.headline: Lone Star Steak sees Q3 net below estimate.

text.p: Lone Star Steakhouse & Saloon Inc said Monday it expects third quarter earnings to be $0.10 to $0.13 a share below analysts estimates.

Continued declines in average unit volumes have reduced margins in the first period of the current quarter, and the company will spend funds on advertising and marketing in the last half of the year, further reducing margins from the levels on which most analyst estimates are based, the company said in a news release.
Comparable store sales are down 11.1 percent quarter-to-date bringing year-to-date comparable store sales to negative 7.7 percent, Lone Star said.

According to First Call, 10 analysts were estimating Lone Star's third quarter earnings in a range of $0.45 to $0.50 a share with a mean estimate of $0.47. The company earned $0.38 in the 1996 third quarter.

"We are hopeful that we can alter the trend in the sales volumes with advertising, but it remains to be seen if any incremental sales will be enough to offset the additional cost of advertising," said Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Jamie Coulter in a statement.

Lone Star owns and operates 230 domestic and 24 international Lone Star Steakhouse & Saloon restaurants; two Sullivan's Steakhouse restaurants; and three Del Frisco's Double Eagle Steak House restaurants.

The company said its average unit volumes have been declining for over one year and the extremely competitive environment for casual dining customers shows little evidence of change in the near future.

Lone Star said it has not advertised in this environment, while most competitors have increased marketing expenditures, which the company believes may have contributed to the loss of customer counts at Lone Star Steakhouse & Saloon restaurants.
Shares of Lone Star were trading off 3/4 to 22.
